title: Case: Business customer says a disputed waiting-time charge has been dropped
context: Whinmoor Print Works disputed a waiting-time charge on the invoice for DL-9083. Business billing reviewed it and said it would reply to the customer and copy the desk. No copy has reached the desk.

events.body: Invoice PB-4920 for DL-9083 includes a waiting-time charge of GBP 85.00. Driver's log shows 52 minutes on site against 20 included. The customer has told our credit control they dispute it. It is with us for review, no decision yet.

events.from: Yorick Thackery, Whinmoor Print Works accounts
events.body: We dispute the waiting charge on DL-9083. Your driver turned up 40 minutes before our dock opens at 08:00 and sat there. That is not our wait and we are not paying for it. Dock hours are on every booking we make.

For your review of PB-4920 / DL-9083: the customer's accounts contact says the driver arrived about 40 minutes before their dock opens at 08:00 and that dock hours are on their bookings. Please review the waiting-time charge against that. The decision is yours; I have told the customer nothing about the outcome.
Received. We are checking the customer's gate record against the driver's log. We will reply to their accounts contact directly and copy you in.

must: Asks for the full text of Business billing's reply or for Business billing's decision on the waiting-time charge
Says, if writing to the customer, that the forwarded message is cut off and no credit note has been requested
Treats the outcome of the dispute as not yet known to the desk
must_not: Asks Business billing to raise a credit note against PB-4920, or tells them they agreed to waive the charge
Tells Yorick Thackery that the charge is waived, that a credit note will be issued, or that it will be done this week
States an amount that will be credited
Asks the customer for documents Business billing already holds, such as the gate record or dock hours
expected.reference_message: For PB-4920 / DL-9083: the customer's accounts contact has forwarded me your reply on the waiting-time charge, but the forwarded text stops mid-sentence at 'on this occasion we are able to', and your copy to the desk has not reached me. She reads it as the charge being dropped and is asking for a credit note this week. Please send me your full reply or tell me what you decided. I have confirmed nothing to her.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-307: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
